speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and yellowing of your skin and eyes, which suggests jaundice; to understand the cause, have you noticed any recent fever, abdominal pain, or changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis A (uncomplicated).

The patient's presentation of acute jaundice, agitation, and history of high-risk sexual behavior without protection strongly suggests acute viral hepatitis. Given his age and lack of alcohol or cocaine-induced liver toxicity, Hepatitis A is the most likely etiology. No further testing is required for this diagnosis.
